ai_jobs.plain_thesis: We think wider AI adoption keeps demand strong for India's IT & software companies over the next 6 months. Across 32 past 6-month windows, an equal bundle of 7 such companies earned about +11.9% on average — ahead of the Nifty's +5.7% — and beat the market about 2 out of 3 times. Nothing here is guaranteed; this is analysis, not financial advice.
ai_jobs.description: More companies adopting AI means more demand for the software and services Indian IT firms sell.
bullets: What drives it: AI adoption lifts demand for Indian IT & software work.
How to act: own an equal bundle of 7 AI/IT companies for a few months.
Main caveat: if the whole market falls, the bundle usually falls too.

yes.summary: If AI adoption keeps lifting demand for India's IT and software firms, owning that bundle directly captures it.

no.summary: If AI doesn't clearly separate IT from the rest of the market, a concentrated bundle adds risk without a real edge — the index is the calmer default.

ai_jobs.caveat: If the whole market falls, the bundle usually falls too.

clean_factors.test: r_i = a + b_mkt·MKT_exMonsoon + b_rain·RURAL_f ; genuine gate b_rain>0 & |t|>=2
clean_factors.method: FWL orthogonalized market control (MKT_exMonsoon) + RURAL_f factor; HAC t
clean_factors.spurious_note: Per the naive-vs-clean test: a name is GENUINE only if it loads positively + significantly (|t|>=2) on RURAL_f AFTER the clean MKT_exMonsoon market control. Names that looked monsoon-linked under the naive (RURAL_f+NIFTY) test but lose significance under the clean control are SPURIOUS (market beta, not rural).
clean_factors.control_factor: MKT_exMonsoon (market with Auto + FMCG sectors purged)
clean_factors.mechanical_loading_note: 73 of 82 'genuine' names are RURAL_f CONSTITUENTS — their ~+1 loading on RURAL_f is MECHANICAL (circular self-loading), so they confirm the thesis basket but are NOT independent evidence. Only 9 names load on RURAL_f significantly WITHOUT being part of it (Asian Paints, Titan, Page, Jubilant, SRF…) — these are the real cross-sectional discoveries: urban-discretionary/quality names that genuinely co-move with rural demand.

expressions.plain_one_liner: A small, defined-risk bet that pays several times your money if the move happens — but you can lose all you put in.
expressions.plain_why: Options give a big, convex payoff for a small outlay when the move is large enough.
expressions.plain_risk: You can lose 100% of what you put in if the move doesn't happen in time.
expressions.option_legs_note: A defined-risk 'call spread' — your loss is capped at what you pay. Exact strikes are set when you deploy.
expressions.exit_period: Held to expiry over the window

option_model.assumptions: Modelled with Black–Scholes at the underlying's realised volatility and a stated risk-free rate on a reference spot of 100; final strikes and premia are set at deploy. Max loss is capped at the debit paid.

entry.note: One lot's net premium — the smallest real ticket for this structure. Final premium is set at deploy.

fintech.plain_thesis: We think India's digital-payment boom helps finance-tech firms. Across 18 past windows an equal bundle earned about +17% on average — but this one is very up-and-down, driven by a few big winners, and it's a young, risky group. Treat it as an uncertain idea. This is analysis, not financial advice.
fintech.description: More people paying by phone (UPI) means more business for payment apps, exchanges and finance-tech firms.
bullets: What drives it: India's UPI/digital-payment boom.
How to act: own a bundle of 8 finance-tech companies.
Main caveat: young, volatile names — a few winners drive the average.

yes.summary: If India's digital-payments boom keeps compounding, the listed fintech and market-infrastructure names benefit.

no.summary: These names are young and volatile with an inconsistent edge — the index is the steadier bet until the pattern proves out.
